fr: La cuisine est à côté du salon.
en: The kitchen is next to the living room.
ipa: /la kɥi.zin ɛ.t‿a ko.te dy sa.lɔ̃/
notes: "à" (preposition, with accent) must not be confused with "a" (verb avoir), even though both sound the same.

fr: Il y a un grand lit dans la chambre.
en: There is a big bed in the bedroom.
ipa: /il i a œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ li dɑ̃ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
notes: The final "d" of "grand" and the final "t" of "lit" are both silent.

fr: Nous rangeons nos affaires chaque matin.
en: We put our things away every morning.
ipa: /nu ʁɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ no.z‿a.fɛʁ ʃak ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Liaison links "nos" and "affaires" with a /z/ sound that has no letter of its own to add.

fr: Les enfants jouent dans le jardin.
en: The children play in the garden.
ipa: /le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ ʒu dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃/
notes: "Les enfants" is linked by a liaison /z/, but the plural "s" of "enfants" itself stays silent.

fr: Mon frère dort dans la petite chambre.
en: My brother sleeps in the small bedroom.
ipa: /mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ dɔʁ dɑ̃ la pə.tit ʃɑ̃bʁ/
notes: The final "e" of "petite" is silent, but it makes the preceding "t" audible, unlike masculine "petit".

fr: Le salon a deux fenêtres et une porte.
en: The living room has two windows and one door.
ipa: /lə sa.lɔ̃ a dø fə.nɛtʁ e yn pɔʁt/
notes: "et" (and) sounds exactly like "est" (is), so context alone tells you which spelling to use.

fr: Ma sœur balaie la cuisine tous les soirs.
en: My sister sweeps the kitchen every evening.
ipa: /ma sœʁ ba.lɛ la kɥi.zin tu le swaʁ/
notes: "balaie" keeps the "ai" spelling even though it sounds like a simple "è".

fr: Les rideaux sont bleus dans le salon.
en: The curtains are blue in the living room.
ipa: /le ʁi.do sɔ̃ blø dɑ̃ lə sa.lɔ̃/
notes: The final "x" of "rideaux" and the final "s" of "bleus" are both silent plural markers.

fr: Il ferme la fenêtre parce qu'il fait froid.
en: He closes the window because it is cold.
ipa: /il fɛʁm la fə.nɛtʁ paʁs.kil fɛ fʁwa/
notes: "que" drops its "e" before the vowel of "il", written as "qu'il".

fr: Nous avons un canapé confortable au salon.
en: We have a comfortable sofa in the living room.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ œ̃ ka.na.pe kɔ̃.fɔʁ.tabl o sa.lɔ̃/
notes: "Nous avons" is joined by a liaison /z/ even though "nous" ends in a silent "s".

fr: La salle de bain est au bout du couloir.
en: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
ipa: /la sal də bɛ̃ ɛ.t‿o bu dy ku.lwaʁ/
notes: "bain" is one single nasal sound, not "ba" plus a separate "n".

fr: Mes parents rangent le garage le samedi.
en: My parents tidy the garage on Saturdays.
ipa: /me pa.ʁɑ̃ ʁɑ̃ʒ lə ɡa.ʁaʒ lə sam.di/
notes: The "ent" ending of "rangent" is completely silent, just like most third person plural verb endings.

fr: On mange dans la cuisine ce soir.
en: We are eating in the kitchen tonight.
ipa: /ɔ̃ mɑ̃ʒ dɑ̃ la kɥi.zin sə swaʁ/
notes: "on" (we, one) sounds identical to "ont" (they have), so only sentence sense tells you which to write.

fr: Le chat dort sur le grand lit blanc.
en: The cat sleeps on the big white bed.
ipa: /lə ʃa dɔʁ syʁ lə ɡʁɑ̃ li blɑ̃/
notes: The final consonants of "grand" and "blanc" are silent unless a liaison occurs.

fr: J'ouvre la porte de la cave doucement.
en: I open the cellar door slowly.
ipa: /ʒuvʁ la pɔʁt də la kav dus.mɑ̃/
notes: "je" loses its "e" before a vowel and becomes "j'" attached to "ouvre".

fr: Il y a beaucoup de bruit chez les voisins.
en: There is a lot of noise at the neighbors' place.
ipa: /il i a bo.ku də bʁɥi ʃe le vwa.zɛ̃/
notes: "beaucoup" combines the tricky spelling "eau" for /o/ with "ou" for /u/, easy to mix up when writing fast.

fr: Nous avons déménagé dans un nouvel appartement.
en: We moved into a new apartment.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒe dɑ̃.z‿œ̃ nu.vɛl a.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃/
notes: The past participle "déménagé" sounds identical to the infinitive "déménager", so the ending must be chosen from grammar, not sound.

fr: Elle a peint les murs du salon en bleu.
en: She painted the living room walls blue.
ipa: /ɛl a pɛ̃ le myʁ dy sa.lɔ̃ ɑ̃ blø/
notes: "peint" ends in a nasal sound with a silent final "t", an irregular past participle spelling.

fr: Nous allons repeindre la cuisine ce week-end.
en: We are going to repaint the kitchen this weekend.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ ʁə.pɛ̃dʁ la kɥi.zin sə wik.ɛnd/
notes: Liaison links "nous" and "allons" with a /z/ sound before the verb.

fr: Les voisins ont fait beaucoup de bruit hier soir.
en: The neighbors made a lot of noise last night.
ipa: /le vwa.zɛ̃ ɔ̃ fɛ bo.ku də bʁɥi jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: "ont" (they have) sounds like "on", so check the plural subject "les voisins" to know it takes "ont".

fr: J'ai acheté des étagères pour la chambre.
en: I bought some shelves for the bedroom.
ipa: /ʒe aʃ.te de ze.ta.ʒɛʁ puʁ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
notes: "acheté" ends in the same sound as the infinitive "acheter", so only the auxiliary "ai" shows it is a past participle.

fr: Où as-tu rangé les clés de la maison?
en: Where did you put the house keys?
ipa: /u a ty ʁɑ̃.ʒe le kle də la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: "où" (where, with accent) must not be confused with "ou" (or), even though both sound the same.

fr: Ma mère a nettoyé toute la maison ce matin.
en: My mother cleaned the whole house this morning.
ipa: /ma mɛʁ a nɛ.twa.je tut la mɛ.zɔ̃ sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: "nettoyé" stays masculine singular because the direct object "la maison" comes after the verb, not before.

fr: Ils vont poser un nouveau parquet dans le couloir.
en: They are going to lay new flooring in the hallway.
ipa: /il vɔ̃ po.ze œ̃ nu.vo paʁ.kɛ dɑ̃ lə ku.lwaʁ/
notes: The final "t" of "vont" is silent, and "parquet" also ends in a silent "t".

fr: Nous avons enfin fini les travaux de la salle de bain.
en: We have finally finished the bathroom renovations.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ fi.ni le tʁa.vo də la sal də bɛ̃/
notes: Two liaisons in a row link "nous avons" and "avons enfin" with /z/ sounds.

fr: Le propriétaire va augmenter le loyer en janvier.
en: The landlord is going to raise the rent in January.
ipa: /lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ va oɡ.mɑ̃.te lə lwa.je ɑ̃ ʒɑ̃.vje/
notes: "en" before a consonant makes a nasal sound with no separate "n" pronounced.

fr: Elle a déjà fini de ranger sa chambre.
en: She has already finished tidying her room.
ipa: /ɛl a de.ʒa fi.ni də ʁɑ̃.ʒe sa ʃɑ̃bʁ/
notes: "déjà" always keeps its grave accent on the final "a" even though nothing in the pronunciation signals it.

fr: Il faut que tu fasses le ménage ce week-end.
en: You need to do the housework this weekend.
ipa: /il fo kə ty fas lə me.naʒ sə wik.ɛnd/
notes: The subjunctive "fasses" replaces the indicative "fais" after "il faut que", an irregular form of "faire".

fr: Ces meubles ne sont pas très solides.
en: These pieces of furniture are not very sturdy.
ipa: /se mœbl nə sɔ̃ pa tʁɛ sɔ.lid/
notes: "ces" (these, demonstrative) sounds exactly like "ses" (his/her) and "c'est" (it is).

fr: Je pense que ce logement est trop cher pour nous.
en: I think this place is too expensive for us.
ipa: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə sə lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ɛ tʁo ʃɛʁ puʁ nu/
notes: "ce" (this, demonstrative adjective) is easily confused with the reflexive pronoun "se", even though no reflexive verb appears here.

fr: Quelle chambre préfères-tu, la grande ou la petite?
en: Which bedroom do you prefer, the big one or the small one?
ipa: /kɛl ʃɑ̃bʁ pʁe.fɛʁ ty la ɡʁɑ̃d u la pə.tit/
notes: "quelle" agrees in the feminine with "chambre" and sounds identical to "quel", "quels", and "quelles".

fr: Bien qu'il pleuve, nous devons réparer le toit aujourd'hui.
en: Even though it is raining, we have to repair the roof today.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil plœv nu də.vɔ̃ ʁe.pa.ʁe lə twa o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: "pleuve" is the irregular subjunctive form of "pleuvoir" required after "bien que".

fr: Les ouvriers viendront réparer la fuite dès qu'ils pourront.
en: The workers will come fix the leak as soon as they can.
ipa: /le.z‿u.vʁi.je vjɛ̃.dʁɔ̃ ʁe.pa.ʁe la fɥit dɛ kil puʁ.ʁɔ̃/
notes: The plural "s" of "ouvriers" stays silent because the next word "viendront" begins with a consonant, so no liaison occurs.

fr: Mon voisin est plus bruyant que je ne le pensais.
en: My neighbor is noisier than I thought.
ipa: /mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ ɛ ply bʁɥi.jɑ̃ kə ʒə nə lə pɑ̃.sɛ/
notes: The string of mute e's in "que je ne le" is barely pronounced in fast speech, but every one must still be written.

fr: C'est le locataire qui doit payer les petites réparations.
en: It is the tenant who has to pay for the small repairs.
ipa: /sɛ lə lɔ.ka.tɛʁ ki dwa pe.je le pə.tit ʁe.pa.ʁa.sjɔ̃/
notes: "c'est" is easy to confuse with "s'est" or "ses" since all three sound the same.

fr: Je doute que ce studio soit assez grand pour deux.
en: I doubt this studio is big enough for two.
ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə sty.djo swa a.se ɡʁɑ̃ puʁ dø/
notes: "soit" is the subjunctive of "être" required after "je doute que", not to be confused with "soi" or "sois".

fr: Quand nous aurons fini les travaux, nous inviterons nos amis.
en: When we have finished the renovations, we will invite our friends.
ipa: /kɑ̃ nu.z‿o.ʁɔ̃ fi.ni le tʁa.vo nu.z‿ɛ̃.vi.tə.ʁɔ̃ no.z‿a.mi/
notes: Three separate liaisons link "nous aurons", "nous inviterons", and "nos amis" with /z/ sounds.

fr: Il semble que les clés aient été oubliées sur la table.
en: It seems the keys were forgotten on the table.
ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə le kle ɛ.t‿e.te u.bli.je syʁ la tabl/
notes: "aient" is the subjunctive of "avoir", spelled with "-ent" though it is pronounced just like "est" or "es".

fr: Ses parents ont refait toute la toiture l'été dernier.
en: His parents redid the whole roof last summer.
ipa: /se pa.ʁɑ̃ ɔ̃ ʁə.fɛ tut la twa.tyʁ le.te dɛʁ.nje/
notes: "ses" (possessive) sounds the same as "ces" and "c'est" but has a different spelling and role.

fr: Nous cherchons un appartement où les charges sont incluses.
en: We are looking for an apartment where the utilities are included.
ipa: /nu ʃɛʁ.ʃɔ̃.z‿œ̃ na.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃ u le ʃaʁʒ sɔ̃.t‿ɛ̃.klyz/
notes: "où" keeps its accent because it means "where", unlike the conjunction "ou" meaning "or".

fr: Il vaudrait mieux que vous répariez la fenêtre avant l'hiver.
en: It would be better for you to fix the window before winter.
ipa: /il vo.dʁɛ mjø kə vu ʁe.pa.ʁje la fə.nɛtʁ a.vɑ̃ li.vɛʁ/
notes: The subjunctive ending "-iez" of "répariez" sounds close to the simple "-ez" ending, so it is easy to drop the extra "i".

fr: Les meubles que nous avons vendus étaient très anciens.
en: The furniture that we sold was very old.
ipa: /le mœbl kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ vɑ̃.dy e.tɛ tʁɛ.z‿ɑ̃.sjɛ̃/
notes: "vendus" takes a plural "s" to agree with "les meubles", the direct object placed before "avons vendu".

fr: La maison qu'ils ont achetée avait besoin de travaux.
en: The house they bought needed renovation work.
ipa: /la mɛ.zɔ̃ kil.z‿ɔ̃ aʃ.te.te a.vɛ bə.zwɛ̃ də tʁa.vo/
notes: "achetée" adds a silent feminine "e" to agree with "la maison", the preceding direct object of "ont acheté".

fr: S'il avait plu, nous n'aurions pas repeint la façade.
en: If it had rained, we would not have repainted the facade.
ipa: /sil a.vɛ ply nu no.ʁjɔ̃ pa ʁə.pɛ̃ la fa.sad/
notes: "si" elides to "s'" only before "il" or "ils", never before other pronouns like "elle".

fr: Bien qu'elle soit propriétaire, elle loue quand même une chambre.
en: Even though she is an owner, she still rents out a room.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kɛl swa pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ ɛl lu kɑ̃ mɛm yn ʃɑ̃bʁ/
notes: "que" elides before "elle" to become "qu'elle", pronounced as one syllable.

fr: Les clés que le locataire nous a rendues étaient rouillées.
en: The keys that the tenant gave back to us were rusty.
ipa: /le kle kə lə lɔ.ka.tɛʁ nu.z‿a ʁɑ̃.dy e.tɛ ʁu.je/
notes: "rendues" agrees with the feminine plural "les clés", the direct object placed before the auxiliary "a rendu".

fr: Si j'avais su, je n'aurais jamais signé ce bail.
en: If I had known, I would never have signed this lease.
ipa: /si ʒa.vɛ sy ʒə no.ʁɛ ʒa.mɛ si.ɲe sə baj/
notes: "je" elides before the vowel of "avais" to form "j'avais", one of several elisions in this sentence.

fr: Il faudrait que le propriétaire fasse changer la chaudière.
en: The landlord would need to have the boiler changed.
ipa: /il fo.dʁɛ kə lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ fas ʃɑ̃.ʒe la ʃo.djɛʁ/
notes: "fasse" is the subjunctive form required after "il faudrait que", distinct from the indicative "fait" though both come from "faire".

fr: C'est le bruit des voisins du dessus qui l'empêche de dormir.
en: It is the noise from the upstairs neighbors that keeps him from sleeping.
ipa: /sɛ lə bʁɥi de vwa.zɛ̃ dy də.sy ki lɑ̃.pɛʃ də dɔʁ.miʁ/
notes: "le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "empêche", merging into a single sound.

fr: Quoiqu'elle ait repeint tout le couloir, l'odeur de peinture persiste.
en: Although she repainted the whole hallway, the smell of paint lingers.
ipa: /kwa.kɛl ɛ ʁə.pɛ̃ tu lə ku.lwaʁ lo.dœʁ də pɛ̃.tyʁ pɛʁ.sist/
notes: "ait", the subjunctive of "avoir", sounds identical to "es", "est", and "ai" but is spelled differently.

fr: Les travaux que l'entreprise a entrepris coûtent plus cher que prévu.
en: The work that the company undertook costs more than expected.
ipa: /le tʁa.vo kə lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz a ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁi kut ply ʃɛʁ kə pʁe.vy/
notes: "entrepris" stays unchanged for masculine plural agreement because the base form already ends in "s".

fr: Il aurait fallu qu'on repeigne la chambre avant l'arrivée du bébé.
en: The bedroom should have been repainted before the baby's arrival.
ipa: /il o.ʁɛ fa.ly kɔ̃ ʁə.pɛɲ la ʃɑ̃bʁ a.vɑ̃ la.ʁi.ve dy be.be/
notes: "que" elides before "on" to form "qu'on", and "repeigne" is the irregular subjunctive of "repeindre".

fr: La décoration qu'elle a choisie correspond parfaitement au salon.
en: The decor she chose matches the living room perfectly.
ipa: /la de.kɔ.ʁa.sjɔ̃ kɛl a ʃwa.zi kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃ paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃ o sa.lɔ̃/
notes: "choisie" adds a feminine "e" because the preceding direct object "que" refers to "la décoration".

fr: Quels que soient les travaux, le propriétaire doit être prévenu.
en: Whatever the work involved, the landlord must be informed.
ipa: /kɛl kə swa.t‿le tʁa.vo lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ dwa.t‿ɛtʁ pʁe.və.ny/
notes: "Quels que soient" requires the plural subjunctive "soient", agreeing with the plural "les travaux".

fr: Si nous avions loué un logement plus calme, nous aurions mieux dormi.
en: If we had rented a quieter place, we would have slept better.
ipa: /si nu.z‿a.vjɔ̃ lwe œ̃ lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ply kalm nu.z‿o.ʁjɔ̃ mjø dɔʁ.mi/
notes: Liaison links "nous avions" and "nous aurions" with /z/ sounds not shown by any letter of "nous".
